summary: Remote WebSocket server obtains interactive shell and file-system control on the installer's host
details: The package runs an agent that connects to a configured WebSocket server and dispatches server-sent messages into full-host control primitives. A `terminal_create` message spawns a PTY (bash/powershell/cmd) on the installer's host and subsequent `terminal_input` messages write their `data` field directly into that PTY, giving the remote party an interactive shell. The same message router exposes handlers for `read_file`, `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `upload_to_dir`, and `git_add`/`commit`/`push`, letting the remote server read, mutate, and exfiltrate arbitrary files under the agent's working directory and push commits from the installer's git identity. An `upgrade_agent` message causes the agent to run `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` and restart itself under systemd/launchd/PM2 with no version pin or signature verification, so whoever controls the server (or the publishing account) can push arbitrary new code onto the host at any time. Installing and running this agent exposes the host to remote shell execution, file read/write, and forced self-upgrade driven by the remote endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
